purpose: Author-side templates for new EdgeBench-style tasks; this is not a SForge task JSON.

terminology.task_family: A reusable problem mechanism, validator, and generator.
terminology.task_instance: A complete agent workspace with a fixed specification, resources, feedback protocol, and scoring contract.
terminology.test_case: One input, episode, workload, or proof obligation evaluated within a task instance.

common_contract.private_information_rule: Keep actual private seeds, labels, references and regeneration secrets outside the agent workspace and its build history; a hash commitment alone is not a substitute for adequate seed entropy.
common_contract.final_selection_rule: Choose one archive by the predeclared feedback-based rule, then evaluate it once on final cases.
common_contract.final_holdout_implementation: New orchestration outside the current standard one-judge TaskSpec; do not treat it as an existing SForge option.
release_gates: Same author seed and pinned dependencies recreate identical task assets.
A trusted feasible reference passes; tiny cases agree with an independent exact oracle.
Invalid, empty, malformed, non-finite, timed-out and forged-score submissions cannot receive valid reward.
Reference, weak and stronger baselines demonstrate useful score separation on repeated evaluations.
Public specification and grader agree on every required constraint.
Feedback reveals useful diagnostics without disclosing target answers.
A long-run pilot shows room for improvement and has affordable evaluation latency.

families.submission: solver.py implementing a published input/output protocol
families.generation: Construct legal routes first, derive compatible demands and service windows, then permute identifiers and hide the construction witness. Validate feasibility after every structural mutation.
families.checker: Independently check every visit, route, capacity, service time and window; compute distance from private canonical input, never from reported cost.
families.feedback: Aggregate feasible-case fraction, constraint-failure type and objective summary; do not disclose hidden routes.
families.score_design: Use independently checked per-case utility with zero for infeasible cases; fail the submission only for protocol/resource violations. Report feasibility and raw cost separately; set score anchors after calibration.
families.long_horizon_design: Require a general solver across diverse regimes so construction, neighborhoods, search scheduling and implementation efficiency remain improvable.

families.submission: Source tree exposing a fixed CLI over JSON event streams
families.generation: Sample a typed semantic specification from a constrained DSL; render the human specification, starter interfaces and reference interpreter from that same object. Maintain an independent test oracle or metamorphic checks to catch shared-generator mistakes.
families.checker: Differential tests against a trusted interpreter, semantics-preserving metamorphic tests, exact boundary tests, then performance tests only after the required correctness gate.
baselines: incomplete operator implementation as negative control
families.feedback: Feature-level pass rates and public minimal counterexamples; keep final event streams unseen.
families.long_horizon_design: Score meaningful feature milestones and their cross-module composition; add performance only once functional coverage has a clear gate.

families.submission: Forward-model and inverse-estimation code using a published sensor-data API
families.generation: Sample physical parameters within validated ranges, solve a trusted forward model, create noisy sparse observations and retain private latent parameters and dense fields. Reject non-identifiable or numerically unstable configurations.
families.checker: Evaluate held-out observation prediction and field consistency; use parameter-recovery scores only for identifiable quantities, with a forward model independent enough to detect simulator artifacts.
families.feedback: Aggregate residual diagnostics and physical constraint checks; avoid exact per-point hidden target errors.
families.long_horizon_design: Progress can come from forward-model accuracy, parameterization, optimization, experimental design and uncertainty estimation.
families.realism_validation: Calibrate synthetic ranges to documented physical scenes and reserve independently sourced real observations when available; report synthetic and real-data results separately.
